mainTopic: Must קדשי קדשים slaughtered in the south come down from the מזבח, and is there rabbinic-level מעילה?
overview: The גמרא asks a new question. Suppose קדשי קדשים were slaughtered in the south instead of the north, and they were already put on the מזבח. Do we take them down? רבה says yes, and רב יוסף says no. The argument is only about the view of רבי שמעון. רבה explains that slaughtering in the south is like strangling the animal, so even רבי שמעון would take it down. The גמרא challenges רבה from a משנה that says there is מעילה on these animals. It answers that this מעילה is only מדרבנן, which means there is no extra חומש payment. It proves from עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן that rabbinic מעילה exists, because dead קדשים still carry it. The גמרא then asks why עולא needed to teach this if a משנה already says it. Its answer begins here and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The question: if they went up on the altar, do they come down?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what happens if invalid קדשי קדשים, slaughtered in the south, were already placed on the מזבח: are they removed?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if they already went up on the altar, do they have to come down?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the offerings from the משנה that were slaughtered in the south. It asks whether, once they are already on the מזבח, they must be taken off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general idea that some invalid offerings, once on the מזבח, are left there (אם עלו לא ירדו). The question is whether an offering slaughtered in the wrong place, the south, gets this protection. The גמרא does not answer yet; it is setting up a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them, a real open question the Sages were unsure about
They went up, meaning they were placed on the מזבח
They come down, meaning they are removed from the מזבח
What is the law?

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If they went up, what is the law: do they come down?
phrases.notes: "They" are the קדשי קדשים from the משנה that were slaughtered in the south, and "went up" means up onto the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: אִי עָלוּ, מַהוּ שֶׁיֵּרְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the משנה's case of קדשי קדשים slaughtered in the south
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether קדשי קדשים slaughtered in the south must be removed if they were already placed on the מזבח

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that they come down. רב יוסף rules that they stay on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says: if they went up, they come down. רב יוסף says: if they went up, they do not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in opposite ways. רבה says take them down; רב יוסף says leave them on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that slaughtering in the south is too serious a flaw for the מזבח to keep the offering. רב יוסף holds that the offering is protected once it is up, like other invalid offerings. The next steps explain where each one's view comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: If they went up, they come down; the offering is removed from the מזבח
If they went up, they do not come down; the offering stays and is burned on the מזבח
Offerings of the most holy level, which must be slaughtered in the north of the עזרה

phrases.english: Rabba says: If they went up, they come down,

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אִם עָלוּ – לֹא יֵרְדוּ.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef says: If they went up, they do not come down.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: אִם עָלוּ – יֵרְדוּ, רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אִם עָלוּ – לֹא יֵרְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to the question in step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה: they are removed. רב יוסף: they stay on the מזבח.

steps.title: The argument is only according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that according to רבי יהודה everyone agrees the offerings come down. רבה and רב יוסף argue only about רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה, don't ask. Everyone agrees that if they went up, they come down. They argue only about רבי שמעון's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument between רבה and רב יוסף. It ties it to a known disagreement between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about invalid offerings that went up on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה is stricter and takes many invalid offerings down, so under his view both אמוראים agree. רבי שמעון is more lenient and leaves offerings that became invalid inside the עזרה on the מזבח. The real question is whether רבי שמעון's leniency also covers an offering slaughtered in the south.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
You should not ask; the answer is obvious
Everyone; here, both רבה and רב יוסף
Where they do argue

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two levels of argument. רבה and רב יוסף are not arguing with רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון. They are arguing about what רבי שמעון would say in our case.

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda, you should not ask,
since everyone does not argue
that if they went up, they come down.
Where they argue is according to Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute of step 2 to the view of רבי שמעון
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, all agree the offerings come down. The dispute is only about רבי שמעון's view.

steps.title: רב יוסף follows רבי שמעון; רבה limits רבי שמעון's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף follows the plain meaning of רבי שמעון, who leaves the offerings on the מזבח. רבה answers that רבי שמעון only said this about blood put on the wrong side of the red line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף holds like רבי שמעון. רבה can tell you: רבי שמעון only said this about blood that belongs below and was put above, or blood that belongs above and was put below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב יוסף's view simply follows רבי שמעון. Then רבה defends his own view by saying רבי שמעון's leniency was only meant for certain limited cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plainly read, רבי שמעון says invalid offerings that went up stay up, which supports רב יוסף. רבה pushes back: רבי שמעון's examples were blood placed on the wrong side of חוט הסיקרא. For example, חטאת העוף belongs below the line, and עולת העוף belongs above it. So רבי שמעון's rule does not automatically cover our case.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said this far, meaning his rule is limited to this case
Offerings whose blood is put below the red line on the מזבח
Offerings whose blood is put above the red line on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rav Yosef holds like Rabbi Shimon.
Rabba can say to you:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon only said his rule
about blood meant to be put below, which one put above,
phrases.notes: "Below" and "above" mean below or above the red line that runs around the middle of the מזבח.

phrases.english: or blood meant to be put above, which one put below,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר לָךְ: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רב יוסף's source and gives רבה's answer limiting that source
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי שמעון's leniency automatically supports רב יוסף in the case of slaughter in the south
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי שמעון's rule was said only about blood put on the wrong side of the red line, not about every kind of invalid offering

steps.title: Slaughtering in the south is like strangling
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that רבי שמעון's cases were slaughtered properly in the north. An offering slaughtered in the south counts as if it was strangled, so it comes down.
steps.simpleTranslation: In רבי שמעון's cases, they were really slaughtered and their blood collected in the north. But here, since they were slaughtered in the south, it is as if they were strangled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his answer. He explains why an offering slaughtered in the south is worse than the cases רבי שמעון was lenient about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון's cases, the שחיטה and receiving of the blood were done properly in the north, and only the blood placement went wrong. In our case the שחיטה itself was in the wrong place, so it is like no proper שחיטה at all, as if the animal was strangled. Even רבי שמעון would agree such an animal is removed from the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth; here it explains what the earlier case was actually about
North, the required place to slaughter קדשי קדשים
South, the wrong place to slaughter קדשי קדשים
It is as if they were strangled, treated like no valid slaughter at all

steps.whatToRemember: רבה says that רבי שמעון only leaves an offering on the מזבח when the שחיטה was done properly in the north. An offering slaughtered in the south counts as if it was strangled, so it comes down. רב יוסף says it stays up, following the plain view of רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that not every flaw is equal. A flaw in the place of שחיטה can make the animal count as never properly slaughtered, which is much more serious than a mistake in where the blood was put.

phrases.english: and really, where one slaughtered them and collected their blood in the north,
but here, since one slaughtered them in the south,
it is as if they were strangled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְעוֹלָם דִּשְׁחָטָן וְקִבֵּל דָּמָן בַּצָּפוֹן, אֲבָל הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's answer by explaining why slaughter in the south is different from רבי שמעון's cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's leniency covers every invalid offering that went up, including one slaughtered in the south
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון was lenient only when the שחיטה was proper in the north. Slaughter in the south is like strangling, so the offering comes down.

steps.title: The משנה says there is מעילה on offerings slaughtered in the south
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that there is מעילה on קדשי קדשים slaughtered in the south. This fits רב יוסף but seems to contradict רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if someone slaughtered קדשי קדשים in the south, there is מעילה on them. This works well for רב יוסף, but it is a problem for רבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to support רב יוסף and challenge רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says these animals still carry מעילה, so they are still fully holy. That fits רב יוסף, who says they stay on the מזבח. רבה said such an offering is like a strangled animal and must come down, so why would the Torah's law of מעילה apply to it?

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most holy level, which must be slaughtered in the north of the courtyard
There is מעילה on them: using them for personal benefit is a forbidden misuse of holy property
It makes sense (according to one view)
It is a difficulty

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה: offerings of the most holy order that one slaughtered in the south
phrases.notes: These must be slaughtered in the north, so slaughtering them in the south makes them invalid.

phrases.english: – there is misuse (מעילה) with them.
Granted, according to רב יוסף it works out well,
but according to רבה it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּה קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבה's explanation from step 5 against a משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that offerings slaughtered in the south are like strangled animals and come down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה applies מעילה to them, they are still fully holy, which suggests they stay on the מזבח like רב יוסף says

steps.title: The משנה means rabbinic-level מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's מעילה is only מדרבנן, not from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it mean that there is מעילה with them? Only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by reading the משנה as talking about a rabbinic level of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, an animal slaughtered in the south is like a strangled animal, so it has no Torah-level מעילה and comes down, as רבה said. The חכמים still made a rule of מעילה on it, and that is what the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not from the Torah itself

phrases.english: What does "there is misuse with them" mean?
– By rabbinic law.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the level of the law in the משנה (rabbinic, not Torah)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's מעילה is Torah-level, showing the animal is fully holy
steps.terutzMaskana: The מעילה is only rabbinic, so by Torah law the animal is like a strangled one, as רבה holds

steps.title: What is the difference between Torah and rabbinic מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between מעילה מדאורייתא and מעילה מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between Torah law and rabbinic law here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the answer it just gave; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way, a person may not benefit from the animal. So the גמרא wants to know what real difference it makes whether the מעילה is from the Torah or from the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between
From the Torah

phrases.english: What is there between Torah law and rabbinic law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical meaning of the answer in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between Torah-level and rabbinic-level מעילה

steps.title: Only Torah מעילה requires paying the extra fifth
steps.stepSummary: Torah-level מעילה requires paying an added חומש; rabbinic-level מעילה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: With Torah-level מעילה one pays an extra fifth; with rabbinic-level מעילה, one does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the difference is the extra חומש payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who commits Torah-level מעילה pays back what he used plus an extra חומש. With rabbinic-level מעילה he only pays back what he used, without the extra fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: They pay
An added fifth, paid on top of the value

phrases.english: With Torah law, they pay an extra fifth;
with rabbinic law – not.

steps.whatToRemember: Torah מעילה = pay the value plus חומש. Rabbinic מעילה = no חומש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra חומש is paid only for Torah-level מעילה

steps.title: Is there really such a thing as rabbinic מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether מעילה מדרבנן exists at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there such a thing as מעילה by rabbinic law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea behind its answer to רבה; the proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה is a Torah law about holy property. The גמרא doubts that the חכמים would create a rabbinic version of it. If they did not, the answer for רבה falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there really...? (a doubting question)
Misuse of holy property for personal benefit

phrases.english: And is there misuse by rabbinic law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the idea used in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה means rabbinic-level מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If rabbinic מעילה does not exist, the משנה must mean Torah-level מעילה, and the challenge to רבה comes back

steps.title: Proof from עולא: offerings that died have rabbinic מעילה
steps.stepSummary: עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן says קדשים that died are free of מעילה by Torah law, which implies they still have it by rabbinic law. The same applies here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: holy animals that died are free of מעילה by Torah law. This shows that by Torah law they have no מעילה, but by rabbinic law they do. So too here, the מעילה is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that rabbinic מעילה exists and uses that to support its answer for רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן specifically said "by Torah law," so there must still be a rabbinic level of מעילה. If dead animals can carry rabbinic מעילה, then animals slaughtered in the south, which are like strangled animals, can too.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy animals that died
They have left the law of מעילה
This shows that
So too here

phrases.aramaic: אִין, דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Yes, as עולא said that רבי יוחנן said:
holy animals that died – have left the law of misuse,
by Torah law.
This shows that by Torah law they do not have it,
but by rabbinic law they do have it.
So too here – it is by rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the animals slaughtered in the south, from the משנה.

steps.whatToRemember: Rabbinic מעילה exists, as shown by עולא's teaching about dead animals, so רבה's view survives the challenge from the משנה.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt of step 10 with a proof
steps.raayaObject: That rabbinic-level מעילה exists, supporting the answer for רבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן: קדשים שמתו are free of מעילה by Torah law

steps.title: Then the משנה already teaches what עולא taught
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה teaches rabbinic מעילה, why did עולא need to say the same idea?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say we already learned in the משנה what עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for עולא's statement, since the משנה (as read for רבה) already teaches rabbinic מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the משנה is read as teaching rabbinic מעילה on an invalid animal, עולא's teaching about dead animals seems to add nothing new. So why did he need to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say we already learned it (in a משנה)

phrases.english: Let us say we already learned this
that עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תְּנֵינָא לְהָא דְּעוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a side question about the proof used in step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה already shows rabbinic מעילה on invalid holy animals, עולא's statement seems unnecessary

steps.title: עולא was still needed: south-slaughtered animals are a special case
steps.stepSummary: Even though the משנה teaches it, עולא's statement was needed, because one might think the rabbinic rule applies only where people do not keep away from the animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though we learned it, עולא's statement was needed. You might have thought that here, people do not keep away from them...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain why עולא's statement was still necessary. The next step finishes the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal slaughtered in the south looks like a proper offering, so people do not naturally keep away from it. You might think the חכמים made rabbinic מעילה only for that reason. That would not prove anything about dead animals, which is why עולא's statement is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
It was needed
You might have thought
Keep away, stay apart

phrases.english: Even though we learned it,
the statement of עולא was needed,
since it could enter your mind to say,
here, people do not keep away from them,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דִּתְנֵינָא, אִיצְטְרִיךְ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: the משנה's case has a special reason that does not apply to dead animals
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's rabbinic מעילה might apply only because people do not keep away from south-slaughtered animals
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא was needed to teach that rabbinic מעילה applies even to dead animals (step 14 finishes the explanation)

steps.title: Dead animals might have been thought to have no מעילה at all
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 13 continues. With dead קדשים, people keep away from them, so one might think there is not even rabbinic מעילה. עולא comes to teach that there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with sacrificial animals that died, since people keep away from them, I might have said there is not even rabbinic מעילה. So עולא teaches us that there is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer for why עולא's statement was needed even though the משנה already teaches rabbinic מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case involves animals people do not avoid, so the חכמים had good reason to add מעילה there. Dead animals are different, because people naturally stay away from them, so there seems to be less need for a rabbinic rule. עולא teaches that the rabbinic מעילה applies even to them.

keyTerms.meaning: People keep away from them
He comes to teach us (the new point is...)
Sacrificial animals that died before being slaughtered

phrases.english: But sacrificial animals that died,
since people keep away from them,
I might say: not even rabbinic misuse applies,
so he teaches us that it does.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל קָדָשִׁים שֶׁמֵּתוּ, הוֹאִיל וּבְדִילִין מִנְּהוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תירוץ begun in step 13 by giving the contrasting case of dead animals.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: עולא's case (dead animals that people avoid) is new compared to the משנה's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since people avoid dead קדשים anyway, the חכמים would not have bothered to make rabbinic מעילה for them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rabbinic מעילה applies even to dead קדשים, and that is the new point עולא teaches.

steps.title: A משנה already teaches מעילה for a dead חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a משנה already teaches that someone who benefits from a dead חטאת commits מעילה. Since dead animals have no Torah-level מעילה, that must be rabbinic. So why did עולא need to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: About dead animals, we also learned this in a משנה: If someone benefits from a חטאת while it is alive, he has not committed מעילה until he damages it. But if it is dead, as soon as he gets any benefit from it, he has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of steps 13–14 by quoting a משנה that already deals with dead animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer was that עולא was needed for dead animals, which the משנה here did not cover. But another משנה speaks about a dead חטאת and says there is מעילה once a person benefits from it. Since dead animals have no מעילה by Torah law, this must be rabbinic מעילה, so עולא's teaching seems unnecessary again.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering
That he damages it (lowers its value)
Any amount at all
He has committed מעילה (misuse of holy property)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה is talking about Torah-level מעילה. A dead animal has no Torah-level מעילה (step 11), so the מעילה in the משנה's dead-animal case must be rabbinic.

phrases.english: About animals that died, we also learned this:
One who benefits from a sin offering while it is alive
has not committed misuse until he damages it.
But when it is dead,
once he has benefited any amount, he has committed misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of steps 13–14 by showing that the dead-animal case is also already found in a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that עולא's statement adds something new for dead קדשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already rules that benefiting from a dead חטאת is מעילה. Since that can only be rabbinic, עולא's teaching seems to repeat it.

steps.title: Opening of the answer: 'You might have thought'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer the challenge with 'סלקא דעתך'. The rest of the answer continues on the next עמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer by starting to describe a mistaken idea one might have had. The full answer comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'סלקא דעתך' introduces a wrong first thought that a teaching comes to correct. Here it opens the explanation of why עולא was still needed, even though the משנה about the dead חטאת exists.

keyTerms.meaning: It might enter your mind (you might have thought)

phrases.english: It might enter your mind
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next עמוד, where the answer is finished.
